details:
**Summary**

Help each user discover suitable worlds they have not visited, with less effort.

Learn from normal browsing, Favorites, and visits, even when the user never submits ratings.

Keep Favorites unchanged and use optional feedback after a visit as an additional signal.

The [For You summary](https://ask.vrchat.com/t/may-29-developer-stream-q-a-summary/48500) describes a personalized experiment. The [world rating announcement](https://ask.vrchat.com/t/where-were-landing-on-ai-in-vrchat/49178/1) describes planned thumbs-up/down feedback. These sources do not specify the internal model or training labels. I am not claiming a defect in the current system.

**1. Keep Favorites useful before and after visits**

A Favorite may mean "visit later," a friend's suggestion, a useful meeting place, or a world the user enjoyed. I would like to keep all these uses. Saving a world does not establish that the user visited or enjoyed it.

Saved but unvisited worlds should remain eligible for discovery recommendations.

Long or repeated visits may reflect conversation, being AFK, home worlds, events, or joining friends. Saves, visits, time spent, and explicit feedback should remain distinct. Missing feedback should not be treated as a neutral or negative rating.

**2. Personalize through normal use, not required ratings**

A shared model could combine world content, patterns in other users' reactions, and each person's browsing, saving, and visit history. The goal is to personalize recommendations even for people who never submit ratings. Optional post-visit feedback would provide an additional signal.

For example, someone who saves scenic worlds and cooperative games should discover unfamiliar worlds in both categories, even if they never submit a rating. Do not reduce all Favorites to one average interest or require an initial questionnaire.

Generate candidates from several interests, collaborative relationships, and new worlds. Respect platform compatibility and content settings. World content can provide an initial basis for recommending new worlds. With no useful personal history, begin with varied compatible worlds.

This architecture can produce personal predictions without prior ratings. Whether it improves recommendations, especially for people who never rate, still needs evaluation.

**3. Avoid simple rules that misread behavior**

Treating every Favorite as a positive rating confuses saving with satisfaction. Broad content tags can also transfer a few reactions too strongly to other worlds. A single negative response should not permanently hide a world or reject its whole genre.

Keeping action types separate does not guarantee better predictions. More behavior types or a larger model do not guarantee improvement either. Both shared learning and user-specific adjustments need tests for overreaction to limited feedback.

**4. Test discovery and effort, not only engagement**

Compare the approach with current recommendations, non-personalized baselines, content-based methods, and collaborative filtering. Test the value of shared history, collaborative world features, and user-specific adjustments separately. Evaluate candidate generation and ranking separately, then the complete system.

Measure actions and time to a new-world visit, visit rates, response rates, and feedback separately. Keep non-visitors and nonrespondents in the relevant denominators. A quick visit does not prove satisfaction. A story or exhibition can be satisfying after one visit.

Check new worlds, uncommon interests, multiple interests, and users with few or no ratings. Preserve diversity and opportunities to discover compatible new worlds. Use information available at recommendation time, without adding later visits, saves, or rating edits to earlier inputs. Voluntary respondents do not represent all users.

**This is a proposal to test against VRChat's existing recommendations; its benefits would need to be evaluated.**

**5. Keep post-visit feedback optional**

Feedback should be voluntary and available only after an actual visit, without repeated prompts. UI details can remain with VRChat.

"Liked it / It was okay / Not for me" is an illustrative alternative, not the announced thumbs-up/down interface. Saving, visiting, and explicit feedback can also remain separate in a two-choice system.
title: Personalized world discovery from normal use and optional post-visit feedback
